en.title: You might not need an agent at all
en.summary: Many teams hand a batch of repetitive tasks to an Agent and let it plan on its own, call tools, and make judgment calls over and over. It looks smart in a demo, but in real-world use it's slow, expensive, inconsistent from run to run, and hard to reproduce when something goes wrong. The author offers a more pragmatic routing approach for anyone building AI automation: decide first which tasks should go to whom, and both cost and stability become far more manageable.

items_all.title: 决策模型深度解析
items_all.summary: 最近 Jev 带火的「决策模型」，把分类做成了一个新赛道：给一段内容、几道问题和候选答案，它直接返回标签与置信度。普通 LLM 要逐 token 生成 JSON，它却能一次并行回答多题，输入便宜、没有输出 token 成本。作者以 Perplexity Decider 为例，拆开了背后的完整机制。想搞懂 Jev 与决策 API 为什么突然火起来，这篇值得细读。

en.title: Decision Models: A Deep Dive
en.summary: The "decision model" that Jev recently popularized has turned classification into a category of its own: give it a piece of content, a few questions and candidate answers, and it returns labels and confidence scores directly. A regular LLM has to generate JSON token by token; this answers multiple questions in parallel in a single pass — cheap input, no output token costs. Using Perplexity Decider as an example, the author breaks down the full mechanism behind it. If you want to understand why Jev and decision APIs suddenly took off, this one is worth a close read.
